Wood is safer than plastic:

"Those using wooden cutting boards in their home kitchens were [CARDINAL] as likely as average to contract salmonellosis (odds ratio [CARDINAL], [PERCENT] confidence interval [CARDINAL]), those using synthetic (plastic or glass) cutting boards were about twice as likely as average to contract salmonellosis ([LAW], C.I. 1.03-3.85); and the effect of cleaning the board regularly after preparing meat on it was not statistically significant ([LAW], C.I. 0.54-2.68)."

The main point is that plastic chopping boards get all hacked up and bacteria find grooves and nooks to hide. 

Wood absorbs the bacteria, but then when the board dries, this kills the bacteria. And wood boards don't get hacked up as easily. 

In the end, it seems wood is better for home for this reason. Just wash and rinse, and I like to clean with a bit of salt and vinegar, then leave to dry.
